trace.error_message: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest deploy) was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. The matching release candidate v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. We rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt partly failed: the orchestrator stopped after us-east, which left regions on mixed versions. A retry finished the rollout in us-west and eu-west. All 3 regions are now on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, look into the orchestrator error during rollback, and find out why v2.3.1 was promoted to production even though its RC failed in staging.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions and opened the SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

**Rollback**
- The latest release, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of about 18%.
- v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.0 had been healthy in production before, so it didn't need change-manager approval.
- The first rollback attempt stopped after us-east because of an error in the deployment system, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1. Rolling back to the same version is safe to repeat, so I retried once and it finished.
- All three regions are now on v2.3.0, health checks pass, and the error rate is about 0.2%.

**Incident**
- I opened **INC-0001** (SEV2, checkout-api). It describes the failure, the rollback (including the failed first attempt) and the follow-ups. Opening it pages the on-call engineer.
- The request to create it timed out, but the incident list showed it had been created. I didn't send it again, so the on-call engineer was paged only once.

**Follow-ups listed in the incident**
- Find out why v2.3.1 failed.
- Look into the deployment system error during the rollback.
- Find out why v2.3.1 reached production even though its test build (v2.3.1-rc) also failed health checks in staging.
